summary: Nomion (Ancient Greek: Νομίων) is the father of Amphimachus and Nastes, the twin captains of the Carian contingent that holds Miletus, Phthires, the Maeander, and Mycale for Troy. Homer names him only as patronym; he has no separate battlefield narrative. Wikipedia treats the house under Amphimachus of Caria.
attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia, "Amphimachus of Caria" · CC BY-SA 4.0

sections.heading: Father of the Carian captains
paragraphs: Iliad 2.867–875 calls Amphimachus and Nastes "the glorious children of Nomion" and leaders of the Carians uncouth of speech. One brother comes decked in gold "like a girl"; Achilles slays that brother in the river and bears the gold away.
Nomion himself is the genealogical root of the Miletan command — not a named fighter in the poem. The atlas id nomion-carion is this Carian house-father alone.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: His sons are amphimachus-nomionid and nastes-nomionid. Keep Nomion distinct from any later historical or zoological Nomion namesakes; Wikipedia's article centres on Amphimachus rather than on a dedicated Nomion page.
